title: Spectral neutrals and compact gutter rebalance for dense tables and chart overlays
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: introduce a spectral-neutral color ramp and a density-aware gutter/radius system to improve legibility in high-density tables and chart overlays while preserving tactile targets on mobile. This ticket scopes token definitions (color ramps, type scale deltas, spacing/gutter adjustments, radius micro-variants, and shadow/elevation tuning) and the migration steps for the component library and docs.

Background: multiple product teams reported reduced readability in dense analytics screens once compact mode was enabled. Existing neutral ramps were designed for larger surfaces and create mid-tone collisions with chart gridlines and table separators. Additionally, our compact gutter math (single spacing scale) doesn't account for row-anchored visual anchors like per-row shadows and control affordances.

Deliverables:
- New spectral-neutral ramp (N-0..N-9) with anchored contrast tokens for overlays (overlay-ink, overlay-sheen)
- Micro-spacing scale: gutter-compact-(xs|sm|md) + row-padding deltas
- Radius micro-variants for dense lists/cards (r-2, r-4) and interactive targets fallback tokens
- Shadow re-profiling: introduce penumbra/light-diffuse layer for hover and selection states; define elevation-compact-0..3
- Migration codemod blueprint and Figma token library update

Constraints & risks:
- Higher contrast improves legibility but can affect brand vibrancy in charts; will provide paired color transforms to preserve hue saturation where needed.
- Reducing gutters risks touch-target regressions on mobile — will require a per-component safeguard in Button/Table implementations.
- Shadow/penumbra changes may look different across OS compositing; we will test on macOS, Win, Android, iOS compositors.
comments: 2025-02-11 — Initial design exploration completed: prototyped spectral-neutral ramp in Figma (file: figma.com/file/Redwood/spectral-neutrals). Feedback: PM wants preserved brand accent for charts; Engineering flagged runtime complexity for per-row shadow calculation.

2025-02-13 — Alignment sync with Eng: agreed to expose density token set as boolean + density-level (compact|comfortable) in component props. Engineering will implement fallback to ensure tap targets >=44px on mobile regardless of gutter token.

2025-02-15 — Accessibility review (Lina Chen): passes AA for body text at compact sizes when using anchored contrast tokens; flagged color contrast for selection states — adjusted overlay-sheen from 12% to 18% over N-2.

2025-02-18 — Design review with Charts team: added chart-specific token chart-grid-muted and chart-foreground-anchor to avoid mid-tone collisions; Charts requested an opt-in token to keep existing palette for legacy dashboards.

2025-02-20 — Engineering PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/3145 — implements token variables and the compact spacing mixin. Raised TODO for codemod to migrate legacy uses of spacing-2 to gutter-compact-sm.
2025-02-21 — PM note (Jordan Blake): recommend phased rollout: 1) internal components and examples, 2) beta toggle for power users, 3) full migration after two-week telemetry review.
acceptance_criteria: New neutral ramp N-0..N-9 added to token registry and published to npm package
Compact gutter tokens (gutter-compact-xs|sm|md) available and used by Table/Card components
Radius micro-variants implemented and consistent across Button, Card, Row components
Elevation-compact-0..3 tokens added and visual regression tests added in Chromatic/Storybook
Migration codemod (js/ts) created and documented; example migration run against one product repo
A11y: body and table text in compact mode meet WCAG AA; selection and hover states reviewed and signed off
migration_plan: Phase 1 (week 1): land token definitions and Figma library; ship tokens package behind feature flag. Phase 2 (week 2): implement component wiring for Table, Chart overlay, Card, Button with opt-in density prop; run codemod on internal admin and analytics dashboards. Phase 3 (week 3-4): beta rollout to 3 product teams, collect telemetry (contrast complaints, visual regressions), iterate. Phase 4 (week 5): full migration and deprecation of legacy spacing tokens with a 3-release sunset. Post-migration: monitor accessibility and product-reported regressions for 30 days.
qa_checklist: Visual: compare before/after across 5 sample dashboards at 800x600, 1280x720, and 360x780 widths
A11y: run axe-core on representative pages and manual keyboard + screen reader checks
Touch: verify minimum tap targets on mobile simulators (iOS/Android) when compact mode is enabled
Performance: ensure tokenization and CSS variables do not increase style recalculation times >5%
Regression: Chromatic snapshots added for each updated component variant
